content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), confidence 0.90.**

**What the document says**
- **§ (c) ASSIGNMENT (p0149):** Licensee may not assign or transfer license rights at all without Licensor's prior written consent (no reasonableness standard, no affiliate or M&A carve-out); attempted assignments are void. No corresponding restriction on Licensor. It also cross-references a non-existent "Section 13.4(a)".
- **Article XX(a) (p0134):** On *any* Change of Control of Licensee, the Agreement and all our rights and licenses **automatically terminate** unless Licensor pre-consents in writing — and Licensor is deemed to have reasonably withheld consent if the acquirer competes with it *or* if Licensor merely "reasonably believes" its interests would be adversely affected. Article XXII also gives Licensor a right of first refusal over our own sale/merger.

**Why it's flagged**
This is the playbook walk-away pattern: a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, combined with a Vendor exit right on our change of control (here even harsher — automatic termination plus an effectively discretionary consent).

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level)**
1. p0149: Licensee may assign without consent to an Affiliate or an M&A/asset-sale successor; other Licensee assignments need consent not unreasonably withheld; Licensor may not assign without our consent and never to a Licensee competitor; a Change of Control is not deemed an assignment and gives Licensor no termination/re-pricing right.
2. p0134: replaced the auto-termination and deemed-reasonable-refusal language with an express statement that a Change of Control does not terminate the Agreement or require Licensor consent — while preserving the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition lead-in used by p0135.

The comment offers the fallback (mutual assignment to successors on written notice with reasonable consent) if Licensor pushes back.
